messages:
elaine-cs: FYI repeating customer escalations for hosted /v1/generate - multiple orgs seeing 503s and large p50/p95 latency spikes starting ~08:04 UTC. I captured request IDs and one trace. Customer said error returns: "upstream error: 503"

maria-support: Which customers? any billing/auth overlap?

elaine-cs: Two customers (acct:redwood-acme, acct:fast-ai). Both on default hosted route, model pinned to rdx-large-1. Fast spike in throughput earlier from a scheduled job (they said). No billing/auth changes.

noah-incident-lead: Tagging incident. ops-bot, create incident and notify eng-runtime.

ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-2167894321 - Hosted inference 503 spike. Paging eng-runtime.

noah-incident-lead: dave-oncall can you triage initial host-level signals?

dave-oncall: Looking at infra metrics now. Node restart spikes on the upstream inference pool around 08:03-08:05 UTC. Containers show OOM killer + segfault patterns. I see repeated: "infer_runner exited with SIGSEGV" then k8s restarted pod.

sanjay-eng-runtime: can you paste one of the container logs? also need model batch sizes and sequence lengths for the failing requests.

elaine-cs: pasted two example request IDs: req=01GZ9X-knv, req=01GZ9X-kny. Customer reports average seq_len ~1024 and bursts with 4096. Batch size default is 8 for their client; they do multi-request bursts during the job.

maria-support: customer provided a stack snippet in their ticket, attaching here.

elaine-cs: ```
[2026-03-15T08:03:12.432Z] infer_runner[pid=4521]: cuda_mem_error: out of memory allocating 1.2GB
[2026-03-15T08:03:12.439Z] infer_runner[pid=4521]: signal 11 (SIGSEGV) at 0x7f8aa2c3
[2026-03-15T08:03:12.444Z] kernel: GPU 0 reset after process killed
```

sanjay-eng-runtime: thanks. That pattern suggests a GPU OOM followed by a segfault in the native attention kernel when trying to recover. We've seen this before when KV cache prefetch + large batch + long seqs blow transient mem.

noah-incident-lead: immediate mitigations?

sanjay-eng-runtime: short-term: 1) add a routing rule to send traffic for pinned rdx-large-1 to the fallback model variant rdx-large-1-q4f (quantized) with lower mem footprint; 2) decrease max_batch_size for hosted pool from 16 -> 4; 3) throttle the customer job if we can (support can ask them to pause). We'll need a config push.

dave-oncall: I can push a temporary autoscaler cap and reduce pool batch size. But pushing routing fallback needs product config change (noah?).

noah-incident-lead: ping deploy-bot to run a quick routing override.

deploy-bot: routing override applied: route/pinned/rdx-large-1 -> rdx-large-1-q4f (weight=100) for tenant fast-ai and redwood-acme. Change ID: ROUTE-2167894321.

dave-oncall: pushing pool config: set max_batch_size=4 on host-pool-upstream-2, and set pod memory limit + eviction thresholds to be more conservative. Doing rolling restart of 6 pods now (one at a time).

infra-bot: rolling restart started for host-pool-upstream-2 (pods: p-12 -> p-17).

maria-support: I messaged both customers asking them to pause scheduled jobs for 20m while we stabilize. They confirmed pause for fast-ai; redwood-acme asking for ETA.

elaine-cs: redwood-acme is on a high-priority SLA. They want earlier update.

sanjay-eng-runtime: while pods are cycling I'll dig into the infer_runner core dump. Uploading gdb backtrace for a failed run:```
#0  0x00007f8aa2c3 in attention_kernel::compute(...)
#1  0x00007f8ab1f0 in kv_cache::prefetch(...)
#2  0x0000555a3b2f in main_loop::handle_request(...)
```
Hypothesis: kernel assumes valid device pointer after an async prefetch; on OOM the pointer becomes invalid and we hit SIGSEGV. We'll add an extra check and a retry path. Patch will take ~2-3 hours to code + test.

noah-incident-lead: Any chance this is caused by a recent runtime change? sanjay?

sanjay-eng-runtime: We shipped a prefetch optimization last week that aggressively preloads KV caches for large seqs. It's been fine in load testing but not with bursty multi-tenant traffic. I'm going to revert that optimization in the runtime Canary branch and cut a hotfix.

dave-oncall: After the route override and restart, errors dropped to near zero for the last 10m, p95 latency improved. Monitoring now.

maria-support: redwood-acme acknowledged lower errors but asked for permanent fix timeline.

noah-incident-lead: Actions/notes: 1) Hotfix runtime to add OOM-safe check in prefetch + revert aggressive prefetch. 2) Postmortem to include capacity guidance for seq_len bursts and recommended per-tenant rate limits. 3) Follow-up with customers on mitigations and offer dedicated or reserved capacity if needed. 4) Add an alert to detect segfault spike earlier (currently we alert on restarts but not segfault pattern).

sanjay-eng-runtime: I'll open PR with patch and request emergency review. PR link: https://git.internal/redwood/infer-runtime/pull/1892 (will update).

dave-oncall: infra tasks: document temporary pool max_batch_size=4, rollback route override only after hotfix validated.

elaine-cs: I'll file the customer tickets with the mitigation notes and ETA.

maria-support: both customers asked about credits for downtime. I'll coordinate with finance to evaluate.

noah-incident-lead: good. Leave this thread open, update when PR merges and when we roll hotfix. Also add postmortem owner.

ops-bot: incident INC-2026-2167894321 status -> mitigated (error rate reduced). Next step: postmortem assigned to sanjay-eng-runtime.

sanjay-eng-runtime: PR created and pushed to review. Will run canary in staging then prod rollout 2hrs after signoff.

elaine-cs: last check: new metrics look stable. p50/p95 trending back to baseline. Closing customer escalations once patch is live.

noah-incident-lead: thanks everyone. Postmortem template will go to #postmortems when ready. :thumbsup:
